# comms-mcp — full LLM reference

Unified fleet comms gateway (v0.1: Telegram Bot API). One portmanteau tool
`comms_ops` with operations send / read_recent / list_threads / status / help.

## Install

git clone https://github.com/sandraschi/comms-mcp; cd comms-mcp; copy .env.example .env
set COMMS_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN (from @BotFather) + COMMS_TELEGRAM_CHAT_IDS (allowlist)
just serve  (or uv run python -m comms_mcp; MCP_PORT=10904 -> HTTP daemon)

## Tools

comms_ops(operation="send", channel="telegram", chat_id="<id>", text="<body>")
  - allowlist-gated; returns {success, outbox_id, message_id}
comms_ops(operation="read_recent", channel="telegram")
  - polls getUpdates, sanitizes inbound, returns recent messages
comms_ops(operation="list_threads", channel="telegram")  -> allowlist
comms_ops(operation="status", channel="telegram")        -> bot + allowlist + stats
comms_ops(operation="help", channel="telegram")          -> setup steps

## Config (env, prefix COMMS_)

TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_CHAT_IDS, TELEGRAM_API_BASE,
DB_PATH, RETENTION_DAYS (7), MCP_PORT, MCP_HOST

## Architecture

FastMCP server; adapters/telegram.py (httpx Bot API); outbox/sqlite.py
(outbox pending/sent/failed + inbound with TTL); sanitize.py (inbound
injection neutralization, email-mcp pattern); Starlette REST /health,
/api/v1/outbox, /api/v1/inbound in daemon mode. Dual transport per
SOTA_REQUIREMENTS 2.3.

## Roadmap

v0.2: Signal (signal-cli) + Slack (Socket Mode); v0.3: WhatsApp (baileys,
self-hosted). All behind the same comms_ops surface. Ports 10904/10903.

## Troubleshooting

- status shows configured:false -> token missing/empty
- send blocked: chat not in allowlist -> add to COMMS_TELEGRAM_CHAT_IDS
- 404 from Telegram -> token wrong or bot token pasted with "bot" prefix
